anomalies.observed: The netlist places J11 pin 1 in both the +5V switched power net and the SBUS signal net. J11 pin 2 is not connected to any net.
anomalies.expected: A connector pin should belong to one net. The SBUS signal net should not be tied to the switched 5 V rail; if J11 is a three-pin SBUS connector, its signal and power pins should be separate nets.
anomalies.impact: RC_SBUS is shorted to +5V_switched, holding the SBUS line high and driving Q5 through R22. This can prevent SBUS operation and may damage connected SBUS devices.

anomalies.observed: The isolated CAN transceivers U10 and U11 have both GND1 and GND2 pins connected to the same system GND net.
anomalies.expected: An isolated CAN transceiver requires separate logic-side and CAN-side ground nets to maintain galvanic isolation. The specification states the board implements two isolated CAN buses through isolated CAN transceivers.

evidence.quote: two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9) through an isolated CAN transceiver

anomalies.impact: The isolation barrier of the CAN transceivers is defeated, so the CAN side is not isolated from the system ground as intended.

anomalies.observed: R34 is connected from /CAN0_N to SW6 pin 1, while /CAN0_P is connected to SW6 pin 4. R35 is connected from /CAN1_N to SW6 pin 2, while /CAN1_P is connected to SW6 pin 3. With the DIP-switch column pairing implied by SW7, this cross-connects the termination resistors to the opposite CAN positive line.
anomalies.expected: Each 120 ohm termination resistor should connect across its own CAN pair: R34 between /CAN0_P and /CAN0_N, and R35 between /CAN1_P and /CAN1_N.
anomalies.impact: When the SW6 termination switches are closed, the buses are cross-terminated rather than properly terminated, and the isolated CAN0/CAN1 buses are coupled through the termination resistors.
